text:
incident-bot: Pager: CRITICAL - GPU ECC error storm on node gpu01 in dedpool 'monarch-vpc-01' (tenant: MonarchHealth). Severity: SEV2. Paging on-call: @ryan. Auto-creation: #incidents thread.
ryan: Ack. I'm on it — will gather impact and start triage. @ana can you join for isolation plan?
ana: Joining. I see repeated AER/ECC counters and kernel OOPSs. Node is flapping PCIe errata and we've got 3 recent task evictions from MonarchHealth jobs.
dedicated-ops: Confirmed. `dedpoolctl node show gpu01 --pool monarch-vpc-01` shows: `state: ACTIVE -> ERROR_ECC_THRESHOLD`. Evac starting: `dedpoolctl evacuate --node gpu01 --grace 30s` kicked off.
elena: Started customer comms: pinged MonarchHealth CS lead (Sarah). Will escalate if they confirm P1 impact. Draft msg ready: "We are investigating elevated errors on a GPU node in your dedicated pool; possible degradation for some workloads. We'll update in 15m." :warning:
sarah-monarch: Received. Customer reports "increased 500s and latency spikes on embeddings endpoint" ~last 10m. They've routed some traffic off their side but want ETA.
ryan: Ok impact confirmed. Plan: 1) Isolate tenant on that node (no new allocations), 2) Drain running pods/allocs, 3) Failover traffic to backup pool, 4) RMA node if hardware fail persists. Ana/dedicated-ops please run the drain and confirm KV cache snapshot for model-serving.
dedicated-ops: Running commands now:
```
dedpoolctl annotate node gpu01 state=DRAINING --reason "ECC spike"
dedpoolctl migrate-tenant --tenant monarch --from-node gpu01 --to-pool monarch-failover-01
kubectl -n dedpool logs pod/gpu01-drainer
```
logs: `migration_start tenant=monarch allocations=12`, `kvcache snapshot complete: 100MB`, `evict: 8/12 succeeded, 4 in grace`
ana: Suggest reducing retries and temporarily bumping batch timeout to avoid tail-latency for surviving pods on failover pool. I pushed a config patch to the route: `routes/monarch/embeddings -> max_batch_wait: 15ms` — rolling update in 30s.
tim: Confirm backup pool `monarch-failover-01` has capacity for the shifted load (2x spare GPUs). Autoscaler won't throttle for next 10m. Monitoring shows CPU/GPU util at ~45% pre-shift.
elena: Sent update to MonarchHealth: "We've isolated the affected node and begun migrating workloads. We expect minimal disruption as traffic fails over; we'll update when evacuation completes or if ETA changes." They ack'd :white_check_mark:.
ryan: Good. @dedicated-ops, mark node with `hardware:needs-rma` in inventory and start power-cycle if ECC persists after drain.
dedicated-ops: Power-cycle attempt #1 returned hardware fanspec warnings but ECC counters still elevated. Marked for RMA and scheduled replacement window 02:00 UTC. Node set to QUIESCED.
incident-bot: Status update: INVESTIGATING -> MITIGATING. Impact: Partial (MonarchHealth embeddings degraded for ~30% requests). Actions: tenant migration, backup routing, RMA scheduled. Next update in 15m.
sarah-monarch: Customer grateful for fast action. They requested an interim SLA credit calc and a timeline for permanent fix.
ryan: Assigning followups: postmortem owner: ana, customer comms owner: elena (prepare credit calc and timeline), infra ops: dedicated-ops (RMA and replacement). Document runbook steps in incident ticket.
ana: Will own postmortem. Early hypothesis: intermittent NVLink/PCIe errors causing ECC storms on this SKU — will collect dmesg, ECC counters, and kernel oops stack for the PM.
elena: I'll prepare the communication and cc legal for SLA/credit evaluation. ETA for a preliminary customer report: 3 hours.
ryan: Thanks everyone. I'll keep channel open for any regressions. If Monarch reports anything new, post here and I'll re-page if we need escalation.
incident-bot: Incident updated (3695006789). Current status: MITIGATING. Last update: 3695010945.
